posts.title: Which tolerances really drive the price
posts.excerpt: Three lines on a drawing that change the quote more than the material.
posts.content:
When buyers ask why a quote is higher than expected, the answer is usually on the drawing, not in the material. A general tolerance of ±0.01 mm on every dimension means every feature must be measured, and often finished slowly.

We look at three things first: tight tolerances on features that do not mate with anything, deep pockets with small inside corners, and surface finishes tighter than the function needs. Relaxing just one of them often cuts machining time by a quarter.

Send us the drawing before you freeze it. A project engineer will mark the lines that cost the most and suggest alternatives, free of charge.

posts.title: Two new 5-axis machining centres
posts.excerpt: More capacity for housings and manifolds from the end of the month.
posts.content:
Two new 5-axis machining centres arrive in our milling hall this month. They take parts up to 600 × 400 mm and will run mainly aluminium housings and stainless manifolds.

With them, we can finish more parts in one clamping, which keeps features true to each other and shortens lead times for complex parts by about a week.

Capacity on the new machines opens from the 26th. If you have a project waiting, send us the drawing now and we will reserve time.

posts.title: What is in our inspection report
posts.excerpt: A short guide to the paper that travels in every box.
posts.content:
Every lot we ship comes with an inspection report. It lists the key dimensions from your drawing, the values we measured on sample parts, the material certificate and the lot number.

First articles get a full report with every dimension on the drawing. For series runs we measure samples at the start, middle and end of the run and keep the data for ten years.

If your quality team needs a different format, tell us once and we will use it for every delivery.
